      "observations": [
        "All 2,327 owned diff lines across 31 paths were read in three contiguous ranges, including every changed test hunk. Both original and fixed accepted conditional metadata were scoped before body output; the additional renamed native receiver paths were also checked and have no Suite-specific branch.",
        "The IDL file, client interface, six callback interfaces, native includes/NS_DECL/NS_IMPL declarations, Rust implementations/safe wrappers, build source list and direct JS QueryInterface/createInstance consumers change together. Interface UUIDs and method shapes remain while IDL parameter names lose the EWS-specific prefix. Concrete Ews classes, exported EWS constructor and EWS contract string remain in this patch; the taskcluster onpush fixture changes only the IDL path.",
        "The shared interface name does not select a transport or establish implementation parity. Both Rust bridges implement IExchangeClient, but the owned Graph create_folder still returns NS_ERROR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED while its folder sync dispatches asynchronous work. The incoming-server factory chooses a concrete contract by server type when Graph is enabled and falls back to the EWS component otherwise. Generated bindings/build compatibility was not exercised.",
        "The MailGlue suggestion to rename its concrete EWS lookup was explicitly rebutted. Owned source keeps @mozilla.org/messenger/ews-client;1 and ewsClient while requesting Ci.IExchangeClient. The accepted endpoint later replaces this path with type-specific ITelemetryRecorder components. That later refactor is separate from the owned interface rename. The historical comment about usual client reuse is not a cache contract: the checked owned factory actually retains mClient.",
        "Documentation removes the EWS-specific root-folder explanation from generic checkConnectivity, leaving the mechanism implementation-defined. onNewRootFolder explicitly assigns first-sync-only behavior to the IExchangeClient implementation. These accepted words match the two different implementation roles; a Done badge alone was not used as adoption proof. The Graph bridge's current doc still names XpcomEwsBridge, so declaration and comment actor must be checked separately; no general prefix policy is inferred.",
        "The direct tests request the same interface from separate EWS/Graph components. The folder test awaits its callback promise and asserts expected create IDs/token, rejects unexpected changes and forwards failures. The server-version helper waits for URL-listener completion. Renamed message callbacks retain separate created/updated/deleted/read-state arrays and onSyncComplete resolution. No new assertions or runtime coverage are introduced by changing their interface names.",
        "The existing updated-message store assertion still reads the separate deletion array in owned and accepted phases. Its expected-behavior message is nonempty but describes more than that receiver checks; existing lesson a81db723e90bef98bf1b7e2a011d9700cf1142e2e07c4dede5f0158eb2daae1c is linked instead of duplicated. The read direct assertions use should messages. Formatting-only reflows and the malformed comment indentation in MessageCopyHandler remain local readability facts, not new behavior.",
        "No protocol synchronization, component instantiation, generated IDL build, ABI check, lint or tests were run. Historical Rustfmt defects, later clang-format task failures without detected defects, Try links and landing with ongoing/failed builds remain reports rather than fresh checks.",
        "Primary 2019005 reuses complete original 809292ea6c344acabde318724f3358ea755e0b2fea8f28cdddd98f54adac5d56, read through current 0–7, activity and actual footer. The author describes the protocol-specific Rust boundary and intended shared C++ reuse. The earlier directory move, this interface rename and outgoing-server work later moved to 2027139 are separate phases. The architecture rationale is not proof that every consumer is protocol-neutral.",
        "D286801's entire creation-to-final timeline and all five actual inline bodies were read. The concrete MailGlue EWS lookup rename is explicitly rebutted despite Done markers. Owned source retains that EWS contract and variable. Documentation feedback is adopted: generic connectivity is implementation-defined and the client implementation is named as responsible for first-sync root notification. The two listener/id-name requests are checked against the full landed diff; the interface and all six callback types change together.",
        "Initial Rustfmt defect reports, later clang-format task failures without detected defects, Try links and the explicit landing with ongoing/failed builds remain historical. They are not a fresh clean formatter/build/test result. Direct tests use the renamed interface but still await callbacks and assert results; shared interface support is not parity, as the owned Graph create-folder method remains unimplemented.",
        "Exact accepted proof keeps later concrete Exchange class names, temporary-client cache publication and dedicated telemetry recorder separate from the owned phase. Existing component-lookup, direct-client completion and message-test assertion findings are linked after scope checks. No source identity is used as proof that all callers are unchanged, and no ABI or protocol execution is claimed."
